## social_media_launch_post

> 1:1 feed-friendly Instagram or X launch announcement post for a new product, with date and CTA.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1024x1024`, aspect `1:1`
**Demo vars:** `templates/social_media/_vars_examples/social_media_launch_post.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A square 1:1 launch-announcement post made for an Instagram or X feed, announcing the product Cove Notes. The image must read instantly in a thumb-scrolling context: an unmissable focal subject riding a clean color block, headline copy stacked above secondary info, and a small CTA chip near the lower edge.
[2. Action] The image works as a single beat — no progression, no carousel intent. The headline announces, the date confirms, and the CTA invites a tap. Hierarchy must survive at thumbnail scale: even at 100px tall the announcement should be readable and the focal subject should remain identifiable.
[3. Scene] A flat designed surface, not a photograph. The background is a saturated solid panel keyed to deep teal #0E7C7B with a warm cream type contrast with one subtle grain or paper-noise overlay for texture. No physical environment. A single decorative shape (gradient orb, soft halftone, or angled band) anchors the focal subject without competing.
[4. Composition] 1:1 frame with safe inner margins of 6%. Top half holds a confident illustrative or product-style focal subject centered horizontally. The lower half stacks: a large announcement headline, a date line in smaller weight, and a pill-shaped CTA chip aligned bottom-right. The grid favors a tight 4-column structure so type stays optically aligned to the subject.
[5. Style] Modern social-feed aesthetic — bold flat color, confident sans-serif type system (one display weight + one body weight), crisp shape language, subtle grain. Palette anchored on deep teal #0E7C7B with a warm cream type contrast plus a paper-white and one neutral ink. No photographic backgrounds, no faux 3D bevels, no glossy reflections.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- announcement: "Cove Notes is here."
- date: "Launching May 14"
- cta: "Tap to listen"

Preserve (edit mode only):
- focal subject silhouette
- accent color block

NO: watermarks, signatures, real famous brand logos, real-celebrity likeness, rainbow palettes, busy stock photography, clip-art icons, faux 3D bevels, lens flare, cluttered floating ornaments
```

## social_media_story_sequence

> 9:16 vertical Instagram-Story-style 3-frame mini-narrative grid stitched into one image.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1088x1920`, aspect `9:16`
**Demo vars:** `templates/social_media/_vars_examples/social_media_story_sequence.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A vertical 9:16 mini-narrative built as three stacked Instagram-Story-style frames, telling a tight three-beat story about a 5-minute morning stretch routine. The result is one rendered image that previews the entire arc — designers will later cut it apart into separate slides, but for review it lives as a single grid.
[2. Action] Across the three stacked frames the beats are: frame 1 — quiet bedroom, alarm dismissed, host stands barefoot; frame 2 — host demonstrates a slow side-bend, breathing label visible; frame 3 — smiling host with coffee, caption Ready for the day. Frame 1 hooks attention, frame 2 elaborates, frame 3 pays off with a clear emotional or informational landing. The hero subject stays visually consistent across the three frames so the eye tracks them as one continuous arc.
[3. Scene] Each frame is a self-contained social-story canvas — flat designed surfaces with bold color blocking, no physical room around them. Between frames there is a soft paper-grain divider band, mimicking the way Story slides separate during review.
[4. Composition] 9:16 vertical canvas split into three equal horizontal bands of 16:9-feeling proportion (each ~33% of the height). Inside every band: an off-center hero element on the left and a stacked text block on the right, with consistent margins and a faint frame counter ("1/3", "2/3", "3/3") in a corner of each band so reviewers can read the order at a glance.
[5. Style] Story-format social aesthetic — saturated flat color blocks, one crisp display sans for headlines, one slimmer companion sans for secondary copy, generous white-space rhythm. Subtle film grain on each frame. Palette is a tight three-color story (one warm hero, one cool accent, one neutral). No photographic backdrops, no glow.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- frame1_caption: "1/3 — quiet bedroom, alarm dismissed, host stands barefoot"
- frame2_caption: "2/3 — host demonstrates a slow side-bend, breathing label visible"
- frame3_caption: "3/3 — smiling host with coffee, caption Ready for the day"

Preserve (edit mode only):
- hero subject identity across frames
- palette continuity across frames

NO: watermarks, signatures, real famous brand logos, real-celebrity likeness, rainbow palettes, photographic backdrops, clip-art icons, lens flare, inconsistent character design, heavy 3D shadows
```

## social_media_thumbnail_grid

> 1:1 YouTube-style 3-up thumbnail grid for previewing alternate channel-cover thumbnail concepts.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1024x1024`, aspect `1:1`
**Demo vars:** `templates/social_media/_vars_examples/social_media_thumbnail_grid.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A 1:1 design-review board showing three alternate YouTube-style thumbnails for the channel "Saltlight Kitchen" stacked as a vertical 3-up grid. The whole image is a single review artifact: each row is one candidate thumbnail in 16:9 form, framed by review-board chrome (channel name banner at top, frame counters at the side).
[2. Action] The viewer should be able to compare the three candidates at a single glance. Each thumbnail must look like a finished YouTube thumbnail in its own right — bold focal expression or scene, big title text, high contrast — but the surrounding board shows they're being judged together, not consumed in feed.
[3. Scene] A neutral light-grey design-review surface with subtle grid lines, not a feed UI. Channel name sits in a header band; the three 16:9 thumbnail frames have soft drop shadows so they read as distinct artifacts pinned to a board. No browser chrome, no YouTube UI, no platform watermark.
[4. Composition] 1:1 frame with 6% outer margins. Top 10% holds the channel-name banner. Beneath it the three 16:9 thumbnail frames stack vertically with even gutters, each labeled "A", "B", "C" on its left edge. Inside each thumbnail: a focal hero element occupies ~60% on one side, the title string occupies the other ~40% in oversized type.
[5. Style] YouTube-thumbnail aesthetic inside a quiet review board. Each thumbnail uses high-contrast color blocking, oversized punchy sans-serif titles with a light text-stroke for legibility, and clearly defined hero focus. The wrapping board uses a calm flat palette so all three candidates can be compared without bias.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- title_a: "A: I tried 5 ramen shops"
- title_b: "B: 30-min weekday dinner"
- title_c: "C: The truth about salt"
- channel_name: "Saltlight Kitchen"

Preserve (edit mode only):
- distinct title per row
- row label legibility (A/B/C)

NO: watermarks, signatures, real famous brand logos, real platform UI chrome (YouTube logo, controls), real-celebrity likeness, rainbow palettes, clip-art icons, lens flare, identical thumbnails across rows, cluttered floating ornaments
```
